critics.summary: MenuPreview's visual upgrade to real food photography is a real win and the URL path is now clean. But the emoji purge was scoped to a single component — HeroBlock pills, FormatShowcase cards, the halal menu page (🌙), the allergens page (164 emojis), and even the new constructor form legend (🥗) still betray placeholder-grade visual choices. Awwwards-level sites do not mix photographic hero blocks with emoji chips on the same page; the visual language is still inconsistent.

Calculator page (/plan/calculator) still appears to require JS — the no-JS path is uneven across the funnel
critics.summary: The catalog <noscript> and constructor SSR form are genuinely useful no-JS conversions — a real Baymard-tier improvement. But the noscript is a link list, not a browsable catalog, and the SSR constructor covers only 12 of ~70 dishes. Combined with non-clickable HeroBlock price pills and a mobile menu carousel with poor discoverability, the conversion path still has too many dead-ends to score above 8.3.

critics.summary: Code-level cleanup is real: Header imports trimmed, MenuPreview simplified, URLs normalized. But the responsive image pipeline for the new /images/dishes/*.png assets is fake — three <source> entries all point to the same full-size PNG, so the 'responsive' markup delivers none of the byte savings it advertises. Combined with lingering AI-photo comments in source and an emoji in the new SSR form legend, this is solid mid-8s work, not portfolio-grade.

fixed: Catalog <noscript> provides 8 anchor links to category pages — no-JS users have a navigable path off the catalog page
Constructor SSR form is a real <form action='/api/quote' method='POST'> with required fields (guests, name, phone, email) and 12 dish checkboxes — submission works without any client framework

9 diet-group number inputs (groupOmnivore, groupVegan, groupHalal, groupGlutenFree, groupNutFree, groupSugarFree, groupDairyFree, groupEggFree, groupOther) let users communicate dietary needs without JS

still_broken: Catalog noscript provides only 8 category links — users without JS cannot browse, filter, or search actual dishes on the catalog page itself; they must click into a category and hope that page is also no-JS navigable
SSR constructor covers only 12 popular dishes — the other ~58 dishes in the menu are invisible to no-JS users; the SSR form is a popular-dishes shortcut, not a true no-JS menu
Other interactive conversion paths (/plan/calculator, /plan/helper, /menu/furshet builder) appear to still require JS — the no-JS funnel is uneven
HeroBlock price pills ('Банкет от 3950 ₽/гость' etc.) are static spans, not links — users cannot act on the price-tier signal without scrolling to find a CTA
No 'add to cart' or 'add to constructor' action on individual dish cards in catalog — even with JS, the conversion path from dish discovery to constructor is multi-step
critics.summary: The two no-JS paths added in W67 (catalog noscript + SSR constructor form) are real UX wins, but they are scoped demos rather than a complete no-JS funnel. A user who lands on /menu/catalog without JS gets 8 category links; if their desired dish is not in the constructor's popular-12, they have no way to add it. The fix improves the floor but does not raise the ceiling.
